_comment: Feature 006 — the committed source of the in-app client changelog. Ingested at agent boot and via POST /admin/content/reingest. Each entry upserts by `slug` (idempotent); entries the seed no longer lists are PRUNED on ingest — seed-owned rows only, including pre-slug legacy rows — so a reset leaves exactly this file. An operator's live Admin -> Updates edit wins and is preserved; an unreadable/empty file never prunes. Client-facing register: keep it tester-friendly, no dev detail.

entries.title: The site now calls itself what it is — Beta
entries.body: The landing page, the access application, and a few app notes still said “alpha” even though you are using the Beta. They now all read the site's real stage, so the beta says Beta and the alpha/testnet build still says Alpha. Nothing about your access or funds changed — this is wording catching up with the product you're already using.

entries.title: Safety answers that never wait on a model
entries.body: Questions about custody — “how do you keep my funds safe?”, “can you withdraw my funds?” — are now answered directly from the system's own guarantees, so they stay available even when the AI provider is busy. The chat's swap suggestion also names the pair you're actually swapping (ETH and USDG on this network).

entries.title: Sparky handles busy moments better
entries.body: When the model provider is briefly rate-limiting, Sparky now waits and retries a few more times instead of giving up, so a busy moment is less likely to end in “something went wrong”. Asking what a vault is paying is also answered straight from the same stored figure the Vault board shows.

entries.title: Asking Sparky what vaults are available now works
entries.body: Asking “what are the vaults available right now?” used to get a generic “no strategy clears your guardrails” reply. Sparky now lists the curated vaults from the same board the Vault page shows, names the current pick, and links the board. The withdrawal receipt also shows the amount you actually withdrew instead of $0.00, and the wallet answer names the token you really hold (USDG on this network).

entries.title: The portfolio's Withdraw action is keyboard-friendly
entries.body: A small accessibility fix: the Withdraw control on a held position is now a real button you can tab to, not just a click target.

entries.title: Withdraw straight from a vault card
entries.body: If you hold a curated vault, its card on the Vault page now shows your position and a Withdraw action that takes you to the withdraw screen with that vault selected. Your Portfolio row links there too. Share amounts on the deposit and withdraw screens are also shown at the right scale, and the withdraw preview names the token you'll actually receive.

entries.title: The deposit acknowledgement tells the truth
entries.body: The confirmation's acknowledgement used to claim it was using your “full idle balance” and called the token USDC — even for a small deposit of USDG. It now names the real asset and the real share of your idle balance, and what stays in your wallet.

entries.title: Deposits into curated vaults can be signed again
entries.body: The confirm screen was waiting on a check that only applies to SparkPoint's own vault, so the sign button never appeared for a curated vault on the beta. It now verifies the deposit directly on-chain and tells you plainly that the policy check doesn't apply to third-party vaults. The confirm copy also names the token you're actually depositing (USDG), and your wallet list now shows the tokens we know for the network.

entries.title: Revenue: every token, in its real units
Behind the scenes: steadier history indexing
entries.body: A fix in how the background indexer tracks its progress across networks — one chain's activity can no longer stop another chain's deposit and withdrawal history from updating.

entries.title: Your beta positions now show profit and loss
entries.body: Once you hold a curated vault on the beta, Portfolio shows its cost basis and unrealized profit or loss, and the value chart starts drawing from your real deposits and withdrawals. Before the first deposit it stays honestly blank — no placeholder numbers.

entries.title: Sparky now sees your beta portfolio
entries.body: When you ask about your portfolio or where to put your funds, Sparky reads the same balances the Portfolio page shows — your idle USDG and any curated vault positions you hold — so its suggestions start from what you actually have, not from a blank slate.

entries.title: Your portfolio now shows your real funds
entries.body: On the beta, Portfolio shows what your wallet actually holds: your USDG balance (at $1 par), your ETH, and any curated vault positions you hold — all read live on-chain. Before you deposit, your idle balance sits right there with a one-tap “Put it to work”. You can also add any token by address to see it in your wallet list.

entries.title: The beta reads in one voice
entries.body: The landing page, onboarding, portfolio, premium and automation screens, and the chat suggestion chips now describe only what's live in the beta — curated vaults, swaps, and your wallet. Nothing you read points at something you can't use today.

entries.title: The beta now speaks only to what's live
entries.body: A copy pass across the app: the vault picker, deposit and withdraw notices, strategies, fees and portfolio now describe only the live curated-vault program, so every label and notice matches something you can actually use today.

entries.title: Updates now reach open tabs reliably
entries.body: We fixed the last piece of the update-refresh flow: the build identifier the app uses to detect a new release was being generated twice with different values, so an open tab could think it was permanently out of date. It is now stable per release, and the app reloads cleanly onto a new build when one ships.

entries.title: Deposit screen fixes, clearer button labels, and fresh builds
entries.body:
The Deposit screen now opens correctly for the wrapped curated vaults on Robinhood Chain (it previously showed a 'not part of the beta yet' notice), and the button now names the token — 'Deposit USDG' — instead of internal wording. The Portfolio note now points to the live curated vaults.

We also fixed app updates not showing up until a hard refresh: new builds now reach an open tab and the update banner can reload onto them cleanly.

entries.title: Real token logos in the swap and vault pages
entries.body: USDG, ETH and the Robinhood stock tokens now show their real logos in the swap picker, the vault cards and your portfolio — no more plain letter circles. The art is bundled with the app (no third-party calls), and logos stay decorative: the verified badge is still what tells you a token is the right one.

entries.title: You can deposit into the wrapped vaults now
entries.body:
The Vault page's recommended vault and every live vault card now open a working deposit flow: the app resolves the SparkPoint wrapper, shows the wrapper's own fee disclosure, and signs the deposit against it. The card also shows the stored curator-scan net APY, labelled as a stored figure, and withdrawals are never gated.

Under the hood this wires the app to the new V3 wrapper fleet — one wrapper per vault, deployed on-chain and verified.

entries.title: Vault page: full-colour pick card and honest wrapper status
entries.body: The recommended-vault card now wears SparkPoint's full brand gradient, and a vault whose wrapper is deployed no longer claims otherwise — it says plainly that in-app deposits for it are coming shortly.

entries.title: The Vault page is card-first — and shows only vaults you can deposit into
entries.body:
Sparky's recommended vault now leads the page in a full-width feature card, and every live vault sits below as a card with its net APY, TVL, withdrawable liquidity and a 30-day trend chart — no more table. Scroll and more cards load in.

We also tightened what's public: only vaults whose SparkPoint wrapper is actually deployed appear here, so every card is depositable today. Vaults still being screened or wrapped are handled in the admin panel and are never shown as 'coming soon'.

entries.title: Under the hood: one clean vault-admission queue
entries.body: The vault admission flow now has a single queue. The old wrapper-request path was retired after the new admission queue went live — the AI can admit a curated vault under the public cooling-off window, and the operator keeps the instant lane. Nothing changes for you: deposits, withdrawals and fees are untouched.

entries.title: Curated vaults: wrapping now follows a public cooling-off window
entries.body:
When a curated vault gets its SparkPoint wrapper, the AI can now admit it on its own — but the wrapper is not deployable until a public cooling-off window elapses (24 hours by default, configurable between 1 hour and 7 days). The operator can admit and deploy a vault immediately, release a cooling-off entry early, or cancel a pending one, and one wrapper per vault is enforced on-chain.

The Trust Center now spells this out, including that upgrades still wait out the 72-hour timelock and withdrawals are never gated.

entries.title: Under the hood: a safer path to automatic vault wrapping
entries.body:
We are upgrading how a curated vault gets its SparkPoint wrapper. Under the new on-chain model, the AI can admit an approved vault on its own but must wait out a public cooling-off window before it can wrap it (24 hours by default, operator-configurable between 1 hour and 7 days); the operator keeps an instant lane to add, release, or cancel a wrapper, and one wrapper per vault is enforced on-chain.

This groundwork is being rolled out now, so the Vault page will say plainly when a wrapper is live. Nothing changes about fees or exits: performance-only above your high-water mark, and withdrawals are never gated.

entries.title: Curated vaults: clearer wrapper fees and upgrades
entries.body:
Wrapped curated vaults now explain their upgrade model up front: every wrapper upgrade must wait out a public 72-hour timelock, a separate multisig can cancel it, and nothing — not a pause, not an upgrade, not SparkPoint — can stop you from withdrawing.

The Vault page also keeps its promise to say exactly where a fee applies: a vault shows the SparkPoint wrapper deposit path only after the wrapper has actually been deployed, and a wrapper is never shown before then. Fees stay performance-only: gains above your high-water mark, never a deposit, a withdrawal, or a losing position.

entries.title: The Vault page is now just the curated board
entries.body:
We removed the “SparkPoint’s own vault” card. SparkPoint is not launching its own vault on this network — the plan is to find strong vaults that already exist here, wrap them in SparkPoint’s own upgradeable wrapper, and bring them to the Vault page for you to use.

When the first vault is onboarded it will appear on the board by itself; until then the page says honestly that there is nothing to show. Deposits and withdrawals always stay in your own wallet.

entries.title: Under the hood: upgradeable curated-vault wrappers
entries.body:
We built the system that lets SparkPoint wrap a curated vault in its own upgradeable wrapper — so fees on gains stay future-proof and fixes can reach every wrapper at once.

Nothing changes on this network yet: there is still no curated vault live here, so there is nothing to deposit. When one goes live, the Vault page will show it with the full fee disclosure, and you will always sign from your own wallet.
